[Father of Babies A & B] and I were sitting with [Mother of Babies A & B] in her room on the labour ward. Her room was the second one in from the double doors leading into the neonatal unit. She was virtually opposite the theatre doors. I remember one of the nurses by the name of [Nurse A] ran past the open door of [Mother of Babies A & B]'s room. I heard her saying something along the lines, 'It's one of the twins'. At the time I didn't know the name of this nurse and I would describe her as a white female in her 40s with dark hair. I was later made aware of [Nurse A]'s name.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Father of Babies A & B] and I looked at one another. I could tell there was a problem and my heart sank. [Baby A] and [Baby B] were the only twins in nursery room 1. I don't know for certain if there were any other twins on the unit at the time. I just immediately thought she was referring to [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B]'s babies. [Mother of Babies A & B] didn't hear what was said as she had one of the midwives from the labour unit with her, talking and checking over [Mother of Babies A & B] after the operation.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The next thing I remember a female member of staff came into the labour suite where [Mother of Babies A & B] was with a wheelchair. I don't remember who that was and they simply said to [Mother of Babies A & B], [Father of Babies A & B] and I, 'Your baby is very poorly', or, 'Your baby has collapsed, we need to take you through'. It was something along those lines.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Father of Babies A & B] and I helped [Mother of Babies A & B] back into the wheelchair and we went straight into the neonatal unit and into nursery room 1/ICU where [Baby A] and [Baby B] both were.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: As we went from the labour unit to the neonatal unit, a member of staff held open the double doors allowing us to go straight through.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The minute I went into that room and I saw that little baby boy, I knew he was gone as he was blue.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: There seemed to be lots of nurses and doctors in the room. [Baby A]'s incubator top was off and open and everyone was desperately trying to help him. As we entered nursery room 1, I remember
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: there was a white stocky male doctor standing off to the lefthand side as you entered the room. He was writing down everything that was going on. I don't know his name.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The room seemed full of medical staff. I am trying to remember. There was what I would describe as a handsome young male doctor consultant; I think he may have been Asian but I can't be certain. This doctor appeared to be taking the lead as he stood over [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The resuscitation attempts carried on as he instructed the medical team.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Mother of Babies A & B] was sobbing uncontrollably at this point, 'Please don't let my baby die, please don't let my baby die'. [Father of Babies A & B] was stood next to [Mother of Babies A & B], completely in shock, he was like a statue, not saying a word.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "After a little while, this male doctor or consultant who was leading the resuscitation of [Baby A] came over to where we were standing and approached [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B] and told them it wasn't looking good.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I cannot remember the exact words used, but he was trying to explain that [Baby A] wasn't responding. [Mother of Babies A & B] continued to plead with the doctors, 'Please don't let him die, please don't let him die'. The male doctor consultant turned around and went back to [Baby A]. They continued to give him adrenaline and carried on with the resuscitation attempts.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The white male doctor standing off to one side carried on writing everything down. All the other members of staff seemed to be assisting in helping but I couldn't tell you what each individual was doing or their role.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I do remember there was a young white female nurse who came over to [Mother of Babies A & B], [Father of Babies A & B] and I. She said something like, 'I'm quite religious and go to church, would you like me to say a few words?' I couldn't tell what you she said but I do recall [Baby A]'s name being mentioned.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Three or four times the male doctor came over to [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B] to tell them things didn't look good.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: He was very nice and tried to explained that if [Baby A] survives, he'll have brain damage and possible further complications. I quietly said to [Mother of Babies A & B], 'You
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: need to let this little baby go now'. [Mother of Babies A & B] was sobbing, 'No, no, carry on, no'.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The doctors carried on a bit longer. I again said to [Mother of Babies A & B], '[Mother of Babies A & B], you have to let this little baby go', and [Father of Babies A & B] actually said 'Yes, [Mother of Babies A & B], we need to let him go'. I think I remember [Mother of Babies A & B] simply nodding her head.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "A few minutes later the medical staff stopped.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I don't exactly remember what happened next as [Mother of Babies A & B], [Father of Babies A & B] and I were in a huddle trying to comfort one other.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The room appeared to empty quickly, leaving just a couple of members of staff. The next thing I remember was this little baby, [Baby A], had been disconnected from all the medical equipment except the tube in his mouth.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: The nurse explained to [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B] the reason as to why certain pieces of equipment needed to remain in place as [Baby A] would have to have a postmortem to establish the reason for his death. I can't recall the nurse's name or describe her.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "One of the nursing staff wrapped [Baby A] in a blanket and passed him to [Mother of Babies A & B] to hold and to cuddle. I don't know how long things took, but we all had a cuddle of [Baby A] to say our goodbyes. Then one of the staff mentioned they would go and get a cool cot to place [Baby A] in. I don't remember any of the names of staff I've described or how many of them were there and what role they had during the resuscitation. The whole evening was a blur.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "To allow [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B] some time together I went outside to phone [Mother of Babies A & B]'s dad to let him know what had happened. I also called [Father of Babies A & B]'s sister and asked her if she could let [Father of Babies A & B]'s mum and dad know about [Baby A].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I then went back inside to comfort [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B].
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "A little while later [Father of Babies A & B]'s mum arrived at the hospital. She stayed about 20 minutes or so. Not long after that, [Father of Babies A & B]'s father arrived at the hospital. He's a very quiet man and doesn't say a great deal.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "Over the next couple of hours I was in and out of the hospital making phone calls to family. When I returned to the neonatal
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: unit, the nursing staff were trying to encourage [Mother of Babies A & B] to go back to the labour ward to rest.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "I don't know what time it was, but [Mother of Babies A & B] flatly refused to leave either [Baby A] or [Baby B] alone. [Baby A] had now been placed into an cot and was alongside [Baby B]'s incubator. One of the nursing staff brought in a large comfortable chair for [Mother of Babies A & B] to sit and rest in as she was refusing to leave her children in nursery room 1. The chair was placed directly in front of [Baby B]'s incubator. [Mother of Babies A & B] held [Baby A] a couple of times but the majority of times she sat in the chair and stared into [Baby B]'s incubator.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "It was around 2 or 3 am when [Mother of Babies A & B]'s dad had arrived at the hospital. He comforted [Mother of Babies A & B] and we all stayed with this little baby throughout the night. The nursing staff brought in chairs for us to sit on. We all tried to persuade [Mother of Babies A & B] to go back to the labour ward to try and get some rest but she just wouldn't leave her children alone and unsupervised.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "The nursing staff had placed a bed in the labour room for [Father of Babies A & B] to get some rest. The nursing staff had suggested moving [Baby A] into the labour room where [Mother of Babies A & B] and [Father of Babies A & B] were resting. Apart from feeling extremely tired, I thought it was time for them to spend some time together with [Baby A] to say their goodbyes.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: I went home, got a couple of hours sleep, returning back to the neonatal unit later that morning. I don't really remember much about that day, that being Tuesday 9 June 2015.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "After making the call to my daughter in Australia, I received a message that she had booked a flight and was on her way to see [Mother of Babies A & B]. The rest of that day was a bit of a blur and I don't really remember much about it. [Father of Babies A & B], [Mother of Babies A & B], [Mother of Babies A & B]'s dad and myself spent the majority of the day with [Baby B] in nursery room 1. It was around shift changeover when one of the midwives in the labour unit almost insisted that [Mother of Babies A & B] needed to return back to the delivery room to rest. They were very nice about it but said to [Mother of Babies A & B] she needed to rest herself. I cannot say who that was or recall her name.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "[Mother of Babies A & B]'s dad and I left the hospital and returned back to my home address. When we got back, I made a cup of coffee and I sat talking to him for a little while before heading off to bed. Just before we left the hospital, [Father of Babies A & B] and [Mother of Babies A & B] were making their way
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: back to their room. I can't be sure if it was this evening or the following evening when [Mother of Babies A & B] moved upstairs on to the maternity ward or whether she was still on the labour ward and back to the delivery room. At some point [Mother of Babies A & B] was moved. I think it was after we had left the hospital.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY

blocks.text: "As I hadn't had much sleep, I dropped off very quickly. The next I think I knew I was woken by my mobile phone ringing. It was [Father of Babies A & B]. I had no idea what the time was but I answered the call the only words I could remember him saying were, 'The baby collapsed, she's really poorly, you need to come'. [Father of Babies A & B] then hung up the phone. I woke [Mother of Babies A & B]'s dad, we both got dressed, and then headed off to the hospital as quickly as we could.
blocks.speaker: MR ASTBURY
